description: Main window: read/write the app-data workspace; native dialogs for import/export; clipboard for copy actions; shell to run Diogenes' perl exporter and pandoc as subprocesses. The fs:allow-exists scope covers onboarding's existence checks only (Diogenes install location and the user-picked TLG folder). The broader read/write/mkdir/read-dir/stat '/**' scopes support a user-picked library folder (shared-folder sync, build spec §11) — the folder is chosen explicitly via the native picker, same trust model as the TLG folder. The pandoc-homebrew/pandoc-usr-local entries pin ABSOLUTE pandoc paths: a Finder-launched .app inherits launchd's minimal PATH (no Homebrew dirs), so the bare 'pandoc' name only works from a terminal launch — the frontend probes which absolute path exists and prefers it (src/lib/export/pandoc.ts), keeping bare 'pandoc' as the last resort. The AI-assist commands (assist_which/assist_run — d7 §B, replacing the former Claude-specific assist_resolve_claude/assist_suggest) are app-owned Rust commands registered via invoke_handler (src-tauri/src/assist.rs) — they are not plugin commands, so they need no shell scope here; core:default covers app commands. Security boundary (d7 §B): assist_run executes a frontend-named ABSOLUTE executable with a frontend-supplied argv array; the binaries actually invoked come from the fixed built-in tool registry (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini) plus the user's explicit custom-command config — the same trust as the user running that tool in their own terminal. The prompt is data (a stdin stream or a single argv element under execve), never shell syntax, so no shell ever parses it. assist_which validates bin_name against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ before it is interpolated into the login-shell 'command -v' resolution rung, rejecting any shell metacharacter without running the shell. This is a small, documented widening of an app-owned command that previously only ran 'claude'.
